brief: Goldman's sales and trading desk called day two of its Communacopia technology conference decidedly bullish. The chain the note draws runs from agentic AI broadening compute demand beyond accelerators to CPUs, to capacity additions and tight supply across wafers, advanced packaging, test and NAND, to the equipment and component outlooks presenters gave. TSMC frames AI as an early-stage multi-year megatrend, argues falling token costs raise consumption rather than cut silicon demand, and says Arizona Phase 1 now yields comparably to Taiwan and is profitable, so roughly 30% of N2-and-beyond capacity sits outside Taiwan in five years, with overseas expansion and the N2 ramp each diluting gross margin 2-3ppts against a 56%-and-above target. Applied Materials reiterated about 40% 2026 revenue growth, Amkor an $11bn 2030 revenue target, SanDisk tight NAND through 2027 and potentially 2028. Software presenters pitched AI monetization: ServiceNow's 4.5x seat value, Salesforce's AE1 at about 5% penetration. Consumer names reported steady spending. The desk notes bottom-up datapoints stay constructive while top-down debates on rates, geopolitics and midterms keep investors from fully re-committing to the AI infrastructure trade.
